construction.implementation_origin: Written from scratch in the isolated build directory

shared_schema.input: Exact fields: schema_version integer 1, synthetic true, feedback array of unique {id,text,severity}; completed_actions array of unique known action names
shared_schema.constraints: At most 1000 entries; trimmed nonempty ids up to 100 characters; nonblank text up to 10000 characters; severity integer 1..5 (booleans rejected). Completed actions describe the top-ranked issue and must be a prerequisite-complete prefix of its path.
shared_schema.output: schema_version, status ok, synthetic true, sentiment {schema_version,issues}, journey {schema_version,status,reason,issue_id,source_priority,next_actions,steps}
shared_schema.errors: One JSON object with schema_version 1, status error, error string; exit 2
shared_schema.validation: One shared validate function validates input, deterministic sentiment evidence/ranking, journey constraints and final envelope. JSON duplicates and non-finite constants rejected.

cross_stage_handoffs: Validated feedback becomes ranked issues with issue_id, severity, sentiment, label, evidence and priority.
Journey consumes the validated sentiment object, selects its first issue, propagates issue_id and source_priority, and uses its severity to choose the prerequisite chain.
Final output is revalidated against the shared source.

behavior.sentiment: Transparent English word lexicon: good/helpful +1, great/love/excellent +2, bad/slow -1, broken/hate/awful -2. Immediately preceding not/never/no negates; punctuation blocks that adjacency. Score is weight sum divided by absolute weight sum, rounded to 6 decimals; zero without matches. Each matched token reports index, effective weight and negation.
behavior.priority: severity*100 + round(max(0,-sentiment)*20), descending; ties by ascending issue id. Caller-supplied severity always dominates sentiment.
behavior.journey: High severity (4..5): acknowledge -> triage -> investigate -> resolve -> confirm -> monitor. Lower severity omits triage. Every action requires its immediate predecessor. Ready journeys contain exactly two distinct sequentially feasible steps. next_actions contains only the currently feasible first remaining action.
behavior.edge_cases: Empty feedback yields unavailable/no_issues. Fewer than two remaining actions yields unavailable/fewer_than_two_remaining with no fabricated steps, retaining a final next action if present. Even positive feedback can represent a severe issue; explicit severity controls ranking.

excluded: Live providers or optional model integration
